newsitem.title: USA: American Phoenix questions Nasdaq critique.
newsitem.headline: American Phoenix questions Nasdaq critique.

text.p: American Phoenix Group challenged on Wednesday the Nasdaq's plans to delist its stock, saying it met the requirements to be listed on the stock exchange's SmallCap Market.
On March 17, 1997, the company was notified that, pending complete review of its initial listing application, effective March 18, the company's securities would not continue to be listed on Nasdaq.

The company said Nasdaq expressed concern that transactions involving the dispositions of the company's assets in connection with a Share Exchange were not at "arms-length" and were not "in accordance with just and equitable principles of trade."
The company strongly disagrees and believes that during the course of the pending review it will demonstrate to Nasdaq that the transactions were at arms length.
The company said it disagrees with Nasdaq's concerns and decision and believes it will satisfy the objective criteria for initial listing on the Nasdaq SmallCap Market.
